assessment.nobel_worthiness: Changed how economists and policymakers understand technology, trade and labour demand. The task-based view of automation and the local labour-market evidence on import competition reshaped the debate on wage inequality, adjustment costs and industrial policy. The work is empirically credible, uses transparent identification, and has wide reach beyond labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task-based approach and the trade-shock evidence. Hanson is a core co-originator of the trade-shock work and Katz of the broader skills and technology literature. Dorn is a major co-author of the trade-shock papers, so the three-name limit forces a hard choice. The task framework also draws on other researchers who are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers date from the early 2000s through the 2010s, with many replications and extensions. The core findings have been tested and refined, including the persistence of trade-shock effects. The topic is mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: Choosing among Autor, Hanson, Katz and Dorn is difficult and the credit allocation is contestable.
Debate continues over the long-run size of the trade-shock effects and the current evidence on AI and automation.
Overlap with earlier prizes on education, technology and wages (Goldin, Card) may weigh on the committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore's 'Credit Cycles' showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It is a foundational mechanism for understanding financial crises, asset-price/credit feedback and balance-sheet recessions, and it underlies much later macro-finance modelling and policy thinking.
assessment.attribution: The core contribution is clearly the Kiyotaki–Moore model from 1997. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the related financial-accelerator and empirical strand, which also builds on work already recognised in the 2022 prize. A two-person award keeps the credit cleanly attributed to the originators.
assessment.maturity: Close to thirty years old, with a very large follow-on literature and renewed relevance after 2008. It is well past the point of needing further confirmation.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2022 prize (Bernanke, Diamond, Dybvig) on financial intermediation and crises.
Whether the committee prefers to include Gertler or Gilchrist for the empirical and applied side.
The model's direct empirical testability is limited, though its influence on later work is not in doubt.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and wage-setting, and the interest-rate-rule framework form the core of modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice. The impact on both theory and practice is very high.
assessment.attribution: This is a large, collective literature. Calvo (time-dependent pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule) and Woodford (the integrated New Keynesian framework) are plausible anchors. Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets are also strong, and any three-name selection will exclude major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of use in policy institutions and extensive empirical and theoretical development.
uncertainties: Attribution is the main problem because the contributions are widely distributed.
Post-2008 and post-2021 critiques of the framework may matter to some members.
Several of the leading figures have previously been mentioned for other macro prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal approach to the open economy, together with the work on exchange-rate determination and the disconnect puzzles, defined modern international macroeconomics. The Foundations of International Macroeconomics and the Redux model had lasting influence on both research and policy.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the natural pair and are closely tied to the framework. Related contributions from others, such as Lane, Gopinath and Gourinchas, are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: The key work dates from the 1990s, with decades of consolidation. This is a very mature body of work.
uncertainties: Some of the exchange-rate puzzles are still unresolved, so the claim to a 'discovery' is weaker than in other areas.
Rogoff also appears in another ballot entry, B013, which raises the question of how his contributions should be weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data was used to measure intergenerational mobility, neighbourhood effects and the long-run returns to policy. This changed public-economics and labour-economics practice and the policy conversation on opportunity. Methodologically it combines quasi-experimental designs with very large register data.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear intellectual leader. Hendren and Friedman are major co-authors on mobility, neighbourhood effects and the policy-value (MVPF) work. Katz is an important co-author on the Moving to Opportunity reanalysis but also appears in B027.
assessment.maturity: The headline results date from the mid-2010s onward. The measurement approach has spread quickly, but some findings, such as causal neighbourhood effects, are still being replicated and extended, and the work is somewhat younger than other candidates.
uncertainties: Relatively recent work, so long-run confirmation and the durability of the neighbourhood-effect estimates remain open.
Credit for the data-access and administrative-data innovations is spread across many institutions and researchers.
Chetty's contributions also span B039, so the committee must decide how to characterise the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed international trade after the 'new trade theory'. It explained exporter premia, within-industry reallocation and a new channel for gains from trade, and it motivated a large quantitative and empirical literature.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman has deep, long-standing work on trade and firm-level extensions. Redding is an important contributor to quantitative spatial and trade models, but his credit for the core discovery is less central. Krugman's earlier prize covers adjacent ground.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years old, with extensive empirical validation and continued use.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier prize to Krugman may reduce the perceived novelty of the contribution.
Helpman also appears in B047, so how his work is bundled across prizes is unclear.
Whether the committee sees the quantitative gains-from-trade work as a separate discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A systematic analysis of how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity affect fiscal policy and economic outcomes. It created a coherent research programme in modern political economics, combining theory with careful empirical work.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the main pairing, with Besley a major contributor on state capacity and accountability. The attribution is reasonably clear, though the literature has many other contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature, from work in the 1990s and 2000s with extensive follow-up.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity.
Persson's role in the Nobel process is a disclosed matter that the committee may weigh, but I do not adjudicate it here.
Some of the empirical results on electoral rules are sensitive to identification assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The diagnosis of weak instruments and the development of identification-robust inference materially improved the credibility of IV-based empirical work. The resulting practices, such as first-stage F-statistics and robust confidence sets, are now standard across applied fields. This is a methodological advance, but narrower and more incremental than the broader findings ranked above.
assessment.attribution: Staiger and Stock (1997) is the key diagnostic paper, while Andrews and co-authors contributed much of the robust inference theory. Moreira, Yogo and others are significant but are not credited in the three names.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with more than twenty-five years of use and extensive consolidation.
uncertainties: The prize has already recognised IV and causal inference (2021), so the marginal novelty may be judged lower.
Credit is split between the diagnostic and the robust-inference theory strands.
Stock also appears in B040, so how his work is bundled is unclear.
